metadata.title: Ergodic Behavior of Diagonal Measures and a Theorem of Szemeredi on Arithmetic Progressions
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Correspondence Principle
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a shift invariant family of bounded complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{Z}$ and $L$ a Banach mean on $\mathcal{F}$. Then there exist a compact metric space $X$, a regular probability measure $\mu$, a homeomorphism $T: X \to X$ preserving $\mu$, and a map $\alpha: \mathbb{Z} \to X$ such that $f(n) = \tilde f(\alpha(n))$, $Sf = \tilde f \circ T$, and $L(f) = \int \tilde f\, d\mu$.
nodes.statement_clean: Any Banach mean on a shift-invariant function algebra on Z is realized by a measure-preserving system on a compact metric space.
assumptions: $\mathcal{F}$ is a shift-invariant family of bounded complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{Z}$
conclusions: There exists a compact metric m.p.s. $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ and $\alpha: \mathbb{Z} \to X$ with $f(n) = \tilde f(\alpha(n))$ and $L(f) = \int \tilde f\, d\mu$

nodes.name: Sarkozy Square-Difference Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be a set of integers of positive upper density. Then there exist $a_1 < a_2$ in $A$ with $a_2 - a_1 = b^2$ for some integer $b$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sets of integers of positive upper density contain two elements whose difference is a perfect square.
conclusions: There exist $a_1 < a_2 \in A$ with $a_2 - a_1 = b^2$ for some $b \in \mathbb{Z}$

nodes.name: Square-Recurrence Proposition
nodes.statement: Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ be a m.p.s. and $f \in L^\infty(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ with $f \geq 0$ and $f \not\equiv 0$. Then the set of $n > 0$ with $\int f \cdot T^n f\, d\mu > 0$ contains a perfect square.
nodes.statement_clean: For nonnegative L-infinity functions on a m.p.s., the set of return times with positive correlation contains a square.
assumptions: $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is a measure preserving system
conclusions: $\{n > 0 : \int f \cdot T^n f\, d\mu > 0\}$ contains a perfect square

nodes.name: Ergodic Szemeredi Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ be a measure-preserving system and $B \in \mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(B) > 0$. For any integer $k \geq 1$ there exists $n \geq 0$ with $\mu(B \cap T^n B \cap T^{2n} B \cap \cdots \cap T^{(k-1)n} B) > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Multiple recurrence: any positive-measure set has some return time at which all of its first k iterates intersect with positive measure.

nodes.name: Topological Multiple Recurrence (van der Waerden)
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space, $T$ a homeomorphism of $X$ generating a minimal flow. Then for any open set $A \subset X$ and any integer $k > 1$ there exists $n$ with $A \cap T^n A \cap T^{2n} A \cap \cdots \cap T^{kn} A \neq \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_clean: Topological-dynamical reformulation of van der Waerden's theorem: in a minimal flow, every open set has a multiple-return time.
assumptions: $T: X \to X$ homeomorphism generating a minimal flow

nodes.name: Diagonal Measure Genericity (k=2)
nodes.statement: Assume $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is ergodic and $(\Omega_2, \mathcal{B}_2, \mu_2, \tau_2)$ is the product as above. The diagonal measure $\nu_2$ is generic for $\mu_2 = \mu \times \mu$ with respect to the algebra $\mathcal{M}_2$ and any sequence $\{M_l, N_l\}$ with $N_l - M_l \to \infty$.
assumptions: $\nu_2$ is the diagonal measure on $\Omega_2 = X \times X$
conclusions: $\nu_2$ is generic for $\mu \times \mu$ with respect to $\mathcal{M}_2$ and any averaging sequence

nodes.name: Generalized Mean Ergodic Theorem (singular measures)
nodes.statement: Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{B}, \mu, \tau)$ be ergodic and $\nu$ generic for $\mu$ with respect to algebra $\mathcal{M}$ and sequence $\{M_l, N_l\}$. Then for $f \in \mathcal{M}$, $\frac{1}{N_l - M_l} \sum_{n=M_l+1}^{N_l} \tau^n f \to \int f\, d\mu$ in $L^2(\Omega, \mathcal{B}, \nu)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Mean ergodic theorem extended to a generic measure that may be singular with respect to mu.
assumptions: $\nu$ generic for $\mu$ with respect to $\mathcal{M}$ and $\{M_l, N_l\}$

nodes.name: Diagonal Genericity for Weakly Mixing Systems
nodes.statement: If $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is weakly mixing, then $\nu_k$ is generic for $\mu_k = \mu \times \cdots \times \mu$ ($k$ times) under $\tau_k = T \times T^2 \times \cdots \times T^k$, with respect to any averaging scheme and the algebra $\mathcal{M}_k$.
conclusions: $\nu_k$ is generic for $\mu^k$ with respect to any averaging scheme and $\mathcal{M}_k$

nodes.name: Weak Mixing of All Orders
nodes.statement: If $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is weakly mixing, then for any $k$ sets $A_1, \ldots, A_k$, $\lim_{N - M \to \infty} \frac{1}{N - M} \sum |\mu(A_1 \cap T^n A_2 \cap \cdots \cap T^{(k-1)n} A_k) - \mu(A_1)\cdots \mu(A_k)| = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Weak mixing implies weak mixing of all orders.
conclusions: The Cesaro average of $|\mu(A_1 \cap T^n A_2 \cap \cdots) - \prod \mu(A_i)|$ tends to $0$

nodes.name: Adapted Algebra
nodes.statement: An algebra $\mathcal{M}$ of bounded measurable functions on $(\Omega, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ is adapted to $\tau$ if the set of $\tau$-invariant functions in $\mathcal{M}$ is dense in $L^2(\Omega, \mathcal{B}_\tau, \mu)$.

nodes.name: Mean Ergodic Theorem for Generic Measures (non-ergodic)
nodes.statement: Assume $\nu$ is generic for $\mu$ with respect to $\{M_l, N_l\}$ and an algebra $\mathcal{M}$ adapted to $\tau$. Then for $f \in \mathcal{M}$, $\frac{1}{N_l - M_l} \sum_{M_l+1}^{N_l} \tau^n f \to E(f \mid \mathcal{B}_\tau)^\wedge$ in $L^2(\Omega, \mathcal{B}, \nu)$.

nodes.name: Tensor Decomposition of Invariants
nodes.statement: Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{B}, \mu, \tau) = (\Omega', \mathcal{B}', \mu', \tau') \times (\Omega'', \mathcal{B}'', \mu'', \tau'')$. Then $L^2(\Omega, \mathcal{B}_\tau, \mu)$ is spanned by functions $\phi(\omega') \psi(\omega'')$ where $\phi, \psi$ are eigenfunctions with conjugate eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Existence of Maximal Kronecker Factor
nodes.statement: If $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, \tau)$ is any ergodic system, it possesses a Kronecker factor $(G, \mathcal{B}_G, m_G, \tau_{g_0})$ such that every eigenfunction on $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, \tau)$ is the lift of a character on $G$.

nodes.name: Kronecker System
nodes.statement: A m.p.s. $(G, \mathcal{B}_G, m_G, \tau_{g_0})$ is a Kronecker system if $G$ is a compact abelian group, $\mathcal{B}_G$ its Borel algebra, $m_G$ Haar measure, and $\tau_{g_0}$ multiplication by an element $g_0$ generating a dense subgroup of $G$.

nodes.name: Subspace of Eigenfunctions $\mathcal{E}(X, T)$
nodes.statement: For any system $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$, $\mathcal{E}(X, T)$ denotes the closed subspace of $L^2(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ spanned by eigenfunctions of the operator induced by $T$.

nodes.name: Triple Average via Kronecker Projection
nodes.statement: For $f, g, h \in L^\infty(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$, the limits $\lim \frac{1}{N-M} \sum \int h(x) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x)\, d\mu(x)$ and $\int_G P_G h(z) P_G f(g_0^n z) P_G g(g_0^{2n} z)\, dm_G(z)$ exist and are equal.
conclusions: The two limits exist and equal each other

nodes.name: Roth's Theorem (ergodic form, k=3)
nodes.statement: If $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is ergodic and $A \in \mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A) > 0$, then $\lim_{N - M \to \infty} \frac{1}{N - M} \sum_{M+1}^{N} \mu(A \cap T^n A \cap T^{2n} A)$ exists and is positive.
nodes.statement_clean: The k=3 (Roth) case of the ergodic Szemeredi theorem with limit positivity.
conclusions: $\lim \frac{1}{N-M} \sum \mu(A \cap T^n A \cap T^{2n} A)$ exists and is positive

nodes.name: Unique Ergodicity Average for Kronecker Systems
nodes.statement: If $\psi(z)$ is a continuous function on $G$ and $(G, \mathcal{B}_G, m_G, \tau_g)$ a Kronecker system, then $\lim_{N-M\to\infty} \frac{1}{N-M} \sum_{M+1}^{N} \psi(g^n z) = \int \psi\, dm_G$.

nodes.name: Continuity of Triple-Convolution Function
nodes.statement: If $f, g, h \in L^\infty(G)$, then $\psi(z') = \int_G h(z) f(z' z) g(z'^2 z)\, dm_G(z)$ is a continuous function of $z'$.

nodes.name: Regular Measure Space
nodes.statement: $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ is a regular measure space if it is equivalent to a compact metric measure space (i.e., compact metric topological space, Borel $\sigma$-algebra, regular Borel measure), modulo null sets.

nodes.name: Disintegration of a Measure
nodes.statement: Given a regular m.s. $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ and sub-$\sigma$-algebra $\mathfrak{D}$, the disintegration is $\mu = \int \mu_x\, d\mu(x)$ where $\mu_x$ is a $\mathfrak{D}$-measurable measure-valued function satisfying $\int \phi\, d\mu_x = \phi(x)$ for $\phi$ $\mathfrak{D}$-measurable.

nodes.name: Ergodic Decomposition
nodes.statement: For a regular m.p.s. $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$, the disintegration $\mu = \int \mu_x\, d\mu(x)$ over $\mathcal{B}_T$ (the $T$-invariant sub-$\sigma$-algebra) yields $T$-invariant ergodic measures $\mu_x$, uniquely determined.

nodes.name: Standard Measure on a Product Space
nodes.statement: A measure $\mu$ on $(\Omega, \mathcal{B}) = (\prod X_i, \prod \mathcal{B}_i)$ is standard if its marginal in each $X_i$ is $\mu^{(i)}$. A function is standard if it is a uniform limit of finite combinations $\sum f_1^{(j)} \otimes \cdots \otimes f_k^{(j)}$.

nodes.name: Tensor-Difference Bound
nodes.statement: Let $f_i, f'_i \in L^\infty(X_i, \mathcal{B}_i, \mu_i)$ with $|f_i|, |f'_i| \leq M$. For any standard measure $\mu$, $\int |f_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes f_k - f'_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes f'_k|\, d\mu \leq M^{k-1} \sum_i \int |f_i - f'_i|\, d\mu_i$.

nodes.name: Compactness of Standard Measures
Standardness of Ergodic Components
nodes.statement: If each $(X_i, \mathcal{B}_i, \mu_i, T_i)$ is ergodic, $\tau = T_1 \times T_2 \times \cdots \times T_k$, and $\mu$ is a $\tau$-invariant standard measure, then almost all ergodic components of $\mu$ are standard.

nodes.name: Y-Module
nodes.statement: A closed subspace $M \subset L^2(X)$ is called a $Y$-module if for each $f \in M$ and any measurable function $h(y)$ for which $h f \in L^2(X)$ we have $h f \in M$.

nodes.name: Y-module Has Section of Norm 1
nodes.statement: If $\dim M_y \geq 1$ for a.e. $y \in Y$, then there exists $f \in M$ with $\int |f|^2 d\mu_y = 1$ for almost every $y \in Y$.

nodes.name: Y-Orthonormal Basis (Finite Rank)
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a closed $Y$-module with $\dim M_y = r < \infty$ a.e. Then there exist $\phi_1, \ldots, \phi_r \in M$ with $\int \phi_i \bar\phi_j d\mu_y = \delta_{ij}$ a.e., spanning $M$ as a $Y$-module.

nodes.name: Submodule Containing Given Functions
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a $Y$-module with $\dim M_y \geq r$ and let $\phi_1, \ldots, \phi_r \in M$. There exists a $Y$-submodule $N \subset M$ with $\dim N_y = r$ containing $\phi_1, \ldots, \phi_r$.

nodes.name: Y-Orthonormal Basis (General)
nodes.statement: Every closed $Y$-module $M$ in $L^2(X)$ with $\dim M_y$ constant ($\leq \infty$) has a $Y$-orthonormal basis. In particular $L^2(X)$ has a $Y$-orthonormal basis.

nodes.name: Module-Plane Cross-Section Equivalence
nodes.statement: If $M$ is a closed $Y$-module with $\dim M_y = r$, then $y \to M_y$ is a measurable $r$-plane cross-section. Conversely, every measurable $r$-plane cross-section arises this way.

nodes.name: Generalized Eigenfunction (relative to Y)
nodes.statement: $\phi \in L^2(X)$ is a generalized eigenfunction with respect to $Y$ if the closed $Y$-module spanned by $\{\phi, T\phi, T^2 \phi, \ldots\}$ is of finite rank.

nodes.name: Subspace $\mathcal{E}(X/Y, T)$
nodes.statement: If $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is a m.p.s. and $(Y, \mathcal{D}, \nu, T)$ a factor, $\mathcal{E}(X/Y, T)$ denotes the subspace of $L^2(X)$ spanned by generalized eigenfunctions with respect to $Y$.

nodes.name: Closure of Bounded Generalized Eigenfunctions
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{E}(X/Y, T)$ is the closure in $L^2(X)$ of the algebra of bounded generalized eigenfunctions.

nodes.name: Power-Invariance of Generalized Eigenfunctions
nodes.statement: For every power $T^n$ we have $\mathcal{E}(X/Y, T^n) = \mathcal{E}(X/Y, T)$.

nodes.name: Fibered Product $X_1 \times_Y X_2$
nodes.statement: Given systems $X_1, X_2$ both having $Y$ as a factor via $\alpha_i$, $X_1 \times_Y X_2 = \{(x_1, x_2) : \alpha_1(x_1) = \alpha_2(x_2)\}$ with $\sigma$-algebra and measure $\mu' \times_Y \mu'' = \int \mu'_y \times \mu''_y\, d\nu(y)$.

nodes.name: Tensor Decomposition of Generalized Eigenfunctions
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{E}(X_1 \times_Y X_2 / Y, T) = \mathcal{E}(X_1/Y, T) \otimes_Y \mathcal{E}(X_2/Y, T)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalized eigenfunctions on a fibered product factor as tensor products of generalized eigenfunctions on each factor.

nodes.name: Bundle of Hilbert-Schmidt Operators
nodes.statement: Suppose $\psi(x', x'')$ defines for a.e. $y$ a self-adjoint Hilbert-Schmidt operator $A_y$ on $\mathcal{H}_y = L^2(X, \mu_y)$ with $\psi(Tx', Tx'') = \psi(x', x'')$. Then the $A_y$ have common spectrum a.e., projections depend measurably on $y$, and eigenspaces form $T$-invariant $Y$-modules of finite rank.

nodes.name: Pairwise-Orthogonal Map Vanishes
nodes.statement: Let $F: X \to \mathfrak{H}$ be a measurable map from a measure space $(X, \mu)$ to a separable Hilbert space. If for $\mu \times \mu$-a.e. pair $F(x') \perp F(x'')$, then $F(x) \equiv 0$.

nodes.name: Generalized Eigenfunctions Over X_2
nodes.statement: If $(X_2, T)$ is ergodic then $\mathcal{E}(X_1 \times_Y X_2 / X_2, T) = \mathcal{E}(X_1 / Y, T) \otimes L^2(X_2)$.

nodes.name: Relatively Weak Mixing Extension
nodes.statement: If $(Y, \mathcal{D}, \nu, T)$ is a factor of an ergodic m.p.s. $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$, $X$ is a relatively weak mixing extension of $Y$ if $\mathcal{E}(X/Y, T) = L^2(Y)$.

nodes.name: Relative Weak Mixing Characterization
nodes.statement: $X$ is a relatively weak mixing extension of $Y$ iff $X \times_Y X$ is ergodic. If $X$ is rel. weak mixing over $Y$ and $Z$ is any ergodic extension of $Y$, then $X \times_Y Z$ is ergodic.

nodes.name: Group Extension
nodes.statement: $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is a group extension of $(Y, \mathcal{D}, \nu, T)$ if there exist a compact metrizable group $G$ and measurable $\gamma: Y \to G$ such that $X = Y \times G$ with $T(y, g) = (Ty, \gamma(y) g)$. If additionally $\mu = \nu \times m_G$, $X$ is a strict group extension.

nodes.name: Reparametrization of Ergodic Group Extensions
nodes.statement: Let $X = Y \times G$ be an ergodic group extension. Then $X$ may be reparametrized so that $\gamma(y)$ takes values in a closed subgroup $H \subset G$ and $\mu = \nu \times m_H$. All ergodic extensions are translates $\mu_{g'}$.

nodes.name: Isometric Extension
nodes.statement: An extension $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ of $(Y, \mathcal{D}, \nu, T)$ is isometric if there exist a homogeneous space $S = G/L$ of a compact metric group $G$ and a measurable $\gamma: Y \to G$ such that $X = Y \times S$ and $T(y, s) = (Ty, \gamma(y) s)$.

nodes.name: Isometric Extension is Factor of Group Extension
nodes.statement: If $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is an ergodic isometric extension of $(Y, \mathcal{D}, \nu, T)$ then it is a factor of an ergodic group extension of $(Y, \mathcal{D}, \nu, T)$.

nodes.name: Characterization of Isometric Extensions
nodes.statement: If $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is an ergodic extension of $(Y, \mathcal{D}, \nu, T)$ and $L^2(X) = \mathcal{E}(X/Y, T)$, then $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is an isometric extension of $(Y, \mathcal{D}, \nu, T)$.

nodes.name: Interpolation of Isometric Extensions
nodes.statement: Let $\{(Z_n, \mathcal{B}_n, \mu_n, T_n)\}$ be a sequence of isometric extensions of $Y$ all factors of $X$. Then there exists an isometric extension $Z'$ of $Y$ which is a factor of $X$ and which has all $Z_n$ as factors.

nodes.name: Distal System (Transfinite)
nodes.statement: $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is distal if it has a sequence of factors indexed by ordinals $X_\eta$, $\eta \leq \eta_0$, with $X = X_{\eta_0}$, $X_1$ trivial, $X_{\eta+1}$ an isometric extension of $X_\eta$, and $X_{\lim \eta} = \varprojlim X_\eta$.

nodes.name: Distal System of Order n
nodes.statement: $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is a distal system of order $n$ if there exists a sequence $\{(X_i, \mathcal{B}_i, \mu_i, T)\}$, $i = 0, 1, \ldots, n$, with $X = X_n$, $X_{i+1}$ an isometric extension of $X_i$, and $X_0$ trivial.

nodes.name: Distal Series $\{Z_n(X)\}$
nodes.statement: $Z_0(X) = X_0$ trivial; $Z_1(X) = Z(X/X_0, T)$ is the maximal Kronecker factor; inductively $Z_{n+1}(X) = Z(X/Z_n(X), T)$, where $Z(X/Y, T)$ is the largest isometric extension of $Y$ in $X$.

nodes.name: Conditional Product Measure
nodes.statement: Let $\theta$ be a standard measure on $X = \prod X_i$ with image $\theta'$ on $Y = \prod Y_i$. $\theta$ is a conditional product measure relative to $Y$ if $\theta = \int \mu_{y_1}^{(1)} \times \mu_{y_2}^{(2)} \times \cdots \times \mu_{y_k}^{(k)}\, d\theta'(y_1, \ldots, y_k)$.

nodes.name: Characterization of Conditional Product
nodes.statement: A standard measure on $X$ is a conditional product measure relative to $Y$ iff for all $f_i \in L^\infty(X_i)$, $\int \prod_i f_i\, d\theta = \int \prod_i E(f_i \mid Y_i)(y_i)\, d\theta'(y)$.

nodes.name: Refinement of Factor Algebra
nodes.statement: If for each $i$ we have homomorphisms $X_i \to Z_i \to Y_i$ and $\theta$ is a conditional product measure relative to $\prod Y_i$, then it is a conditional product measure relative to $\prod Z_i$.

nodes.name: Isomorphism via Conditional Product
nodes.statement: If $\theta$ is a conditional product measure relative to $Y$ then $\hat\alpha: X \to \hat X$ defined via the natural inclusion is a measure-preserving isomorphism of $X$ with $\hat X$.

nodes.name: Ergodic Components of Conditional Product Measures
nodes.statement: Assume $(X_i, \mathcal{B}_i, \mu^{(i)}, T)$ is an extension of an ergodic m.p.s. $(Y_i, \mathcal{D}_i, \nu^{(i)}, T)$ and $\theta$ is a $T$-invariant standard measure on $X = \prod X_i$ that is a conditional product measure relative to $Y = \prod Y_i$. Then almost all ergodic components of $\theta$ are conditional product measures relative to $\hat Y = \prod \hat Y_i$ (where $\hat Y_i = Z(X_i/Y_i, T)$).

nodes.name: Ergodic Components of CP Measures (Quasi-Ergodic)
nodes.statement: Assume each $(Y_i, \mathcal{D}_i, \nu^{(i)}, T)$ is a quasi-ergodic factor of $(X_i, \mathcal{B}_i, \mu^{(i)}, T)$. Let $\theta$ be a $T$-invariant standard measure on $X = \prod X_i$ which is a conditional product measure relative to $Y = \prod Y_i$. Then almost all ergodic components of $\theta$ are conditional product measures relative to $\hat Y = \prod \hat Y_i$.

nodes.name: Diagonal Measure $\mu_d^k$ on $X^k$
nodes.statement: For ergodic $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ and $\tau_k = T \times T^2 \times \cdots \times T^k$, the diagonal measure $\mu_d^k$ on $X^k$ satisfies $\int \prod f_i(x_i)\, d\mu_d^k = \int \prod f_i(x)\, d\mu(x)$.

nodes.name: Projection of Generic Limit
nodes.statement: $\pi_k(\mu_*^k) = \mu_*^{k-1}$, where $\pi_k$ is the projection from $X^k$ onto the last $k-1$ coordinates and $\mu_*^k$ is the generic limit of $\mu_d^k$.

nodes.name: Standard Measure Defined Over a Factor
nodes.statement: Let $(Y, \mathcal{D}, \nu, T)$ be a factor of $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$. A standard measure $\theta$ on $(X^k, \mathcal{B}^k)$ is defined over $Y$ if $\theta$ is a conditional product measure in $X^k$ relative to $Y^k$.

nodes.name: Diagonal Generic Limit Defined Over $Z_{k-2}$
nodes.statement: $\mu_*^k$ is defined over $Z_{k-2}(X)$, where $\{Z_n(X)\}$ is the distal series of $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The k-fold diagonal generic limit lives over the (k-2)-step distal factor.

nodes.name: Reduction to Finite-Order Distal Systems
nodes.statement: If $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is a distal system of finite order, $\mu_d^k$ and $\mu_*^k$ defined as above, and $f \in L^\infty(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ nonnegative not a.e. zero, then $\int f(x_1) f(x_2) \cdots f(x_k)\, d\mu_*^k > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: For finite-order distal systems, the generic limit measure assigns positive mass to nonnegative product functions.

nodes.name: Null Family $\mathcal{N}(\theta)$
nodes.statement: Let $\theta$ be a standard measure on $\hat X = X^k$. $\mathcal{N}(\theta)$ consists of all $k$-tuples $f_1, \ldots, f_k \in L^\infty(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ with $0 \leq f_i \leq 1$ and $\int f_1(x_1) \cdots f_k(x_k)\, d\theta = 0$.

nodes.name: Order $\theta' \prec \theta''$
nodes.statement: For standard measures $\theta', \theta''$ on $\hat X = X^k$, $\theta' \prec \theta''$ means $\mathcal{N}(\theta'') \subset \mathcal{N}(\theta')$.

nodes.name: Supporting Set
nodes.statement: $S$ is a supporting set of standard measure $\theta$ on $\hat X$ if $\theta(S) = 1$ and for every $(f_1, \ldots, f_k) \in \mathcal{N}(\theta)$ the product $f_1(x_1) \cdots f_k(x_k)$ vanishes on $S$ except on a set of standard measure 0.

nodes.name: Existence of Supporting Set
nodes.statement: Every standard measure has a supporting set.

nodes.name: Support Inclusion Implies Order
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{S}(\theta') \subset \mathcal{S}(\theta'')$ then $\theta' \prec \theta''$.

nodes.name: Diagonal as Support of $\mu_d^k$
nodes.statement: The diagonal is a supporting set of $\mu_d^k$.

nodes.name: Distal Multiple Recurrence (Main)
nodes.statement: If $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is an ergodic distal system of finite order, $\mu_d^k$ the diagonal measure on $\hat X = X^k$, and for some averaging scheme $\mu_d^k$ is generic for $\mu_*^k$ under $\tau_k = T \times T^2 \times \cdots \times T^k$, then $\mu_d^k \prec \mu_*^k$.
nodes.statement_clean: For ergodic finite-order distal systems, the diagonal measure is dominated (in the support order) by the limiting measure.

nodes.name: Group Extension Step (Induction Step for Distal Recurrence)
nodes.statement: Assume Theorem 11.3 valid for a system $(Y, \mathcal{D}, \nu, T)$ and let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ be a strict group extension of $(Y, \mathcal{D}, \nu, T)$. Then Theorem 11.3 is also valid for $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$.

nodes.name: Convolution $\lambda * \theta$
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda$ be a measure on $\hat G = G^k$ and $\theta$ a standard measure on $X^k$. Then $\lambda * \theta$ is defined by $\int f(x)\, d(\lambda * \theta)(x) = \iint f(\rho_g(x))\, d\lambda(g)\, d\theta(x)$.

nodes.name: Diagonal Dominated by Haar Convolution
nodes.statement: If $m_G$ denotes Haar measure on $G$ then $\mu_d^k \prec m_G * \mu_*^k$.

nodes.name: Support of Convex Combination
nodes.statement: For any two standard measures $\theta', \theta''$ and $0 < p < 1$, $\mathcal{S}_0(p\theta' + (1-p)\theta'') = \mathcal{S}_0(\theta') \cup \mathcal{S}_0(\theta'')$.

nodes.name: T-Invariance of Convolution Support
nodes.statement: For any measure $\lambda$ on $\hat G$, $\mathcal{S}_0(\lambda * \mu_*^k)$ is $T$-invariant.

nodes.name: Convex Decomposition of Convolution Order
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda$ be a non-trivial convex combination of measures $\lambda_1, \lambda_2$ on $\hat G$. If $\mu_d^k \prec \lambda * \mu_*^k$ then either $\mu_d^k \prec \lambda_1 * \mu_*^k$ or $\mu_d^k \prec \lambda_2 * \mu_*^k$.

nodes.name: Closure Property of Set $E$
nodes.statement: $E = \{\xi \in \hat G : \exists \text{arbitrarily small nbhds } V \text{ of } \xi \text{ with } \mu_d^k \prec \lambda_V * \mu_*^k\}$ is a non-empty closed semi-group of $\hat G$, hence a group containing the identity.

nodes.name: Identity-Neighborhood Domination
nodes.statement: For any neighborhood $V$ of the identity in $\hat G$, $\mu_d^k \prec \lambda_V * \mu_*^k$.

nodes.name: Diagonal Subgroup Convolution Identity
nodes.statement: Let $G_\Delta \subset \hat G$ denote the diagonal subgroup and $\lambda_\Delta$ Haar measure on $G_\Delta$. Then $\lambda_\Delta * \mu_*^k = \mu_*^k$.

nodes.name: Multiple Recurrence (Final Form)
nodes.statement: If $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ is an ergodic system, $f \in L^\infty(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ with $f \geq 0$ and $f$ not a.e. 0, then for any $k$, $\liminf_{N - M \to \infty} \frac{1}{N - M} \sum_{M+1}^{N} \int f(x) f(T^n x) \cdots f(T^{(k-1)n} x)\, d\mu(x) > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Final form of multiple recurrence: Cesaro-positive integral of f times its powers under iterated T.

nodes.name: Szemeredi's Theorem on Arithmetic Progressions
nodes.statement: Any subset of $\mathbb{Z}$ of positive upper density contains arithmetic progressions of arbitrary finite length.
nodes.origin_citation: Szemeredi 1975 (this paper provides the ergodic-theoretic proof)

nodes.name: van der Waerden's Theorem
nodes.statement: If the integers are partitioned into finitely many subsets, one subset possesses arithmetic progressions of arbitrary finite length.

nodes.name: Roth's Theorem
nodes.statement: Any subset of $\mathbb{Z}$ of positive upper density contains arithmetic progressions of length 3.

nodes.name: Mean Ergodic Theorem (von Neumann)
nodes.statement: For a m.p.s. $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ and $f \in L^2(X)$, $\frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=1}^N T^n f \to E(f \mid \mathcal{B}_T)$ in $L^2$ where $\mathcal{B}_T$ is the $\sigma$-algebra of $T$-invariant sets.

nodes.name: Weyl Equidistribution of $q^2 \alpha$
nodes.statement: For irrational $\alpha / \pi$, the sequence $q^2 \alpha$ is equidistributed modulo $2\pi$.

nodes.name: Spectral Theorem (for Unitary Operators)
nodes.statement: For a m.p.s. $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ and $f \in L^2$, $\int f \cdot T^n f\, d\mu = \int_{-\pi}^{\pi} e^{in\theta}\, dp(\theta)$ for some positive measure $p$.

nodes.name: Proof of Square-Recurrence Proposition
nodes.statement: Apply spectral theorem to $\int f \cdot T^n f\, d\mu = \int e^{in\theta} dp(\theta)$, decompose $p$ into point mass at 0, finite rational-multiple part, and remainder; use Weyl equidistribution to derive contradiction with assumption that no perfect square works.

nodes.name: Spectral Representation
nodes.statement: By the spectral theorem, $\int f \cdot T^n f\, d\mu = \int_{-\pi}^{\pi} e^{in\theta}\, dp(\theta)$ for a positive measure $p$.

nodes.name: Compute Point Mass at 0
nodes.statement: By the mean ergodic theorem, $\frac{1}{N}\sum T^n f \to E(f \mid \phi)$, so averaging the spectral identity yields $p(\{0\}) = E(E(f \mid \phi)^2) > 0$.

nodes.name: Decompose Spectral Measure
nodes.statement: Write $p = p_0 + p_1 + p_2$ where $p_0$ is point mass at 0, $p_1$ is supported on rational multiples of $\pi$ (finitely many of form $2j\pi/m$), $p_2$ has small mass on rational multiples of $\pi$.

nodes.name: Apply Weyl Equidistribution
nodes.statement: Choose $n = m^2 q^2$, average over $1 \leq q \leq N$. Weyl's theorem on equidistribution of $q^2 \alpha$ shows $p_2$ contributes at most $\epsilon$, while $p_1$ vanishes for these $n$, contradicting $p(\{0\}) > 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Diagonal Genericity for Weak Mixing
nodes.statement: By induction on $k$. Base $k=2$ is Lemma 2.1. Induction step uses Theorem 2.2 (mean ergodic for generic measures) on the ergodic system $(\Omega_k, \mathcal{B}_k, \mu_k, \tau_k)$.

nodes.name: Base Case k=2
nodes.statement: By Lemma 2.1 ($\nu_2$ generic for $\mu \times \mu$).

nodes.name: Apply Mean Ergodic Theorem
nodes.statement: Since $(\Omega_k, \mathcal{B}_k, \mu_k, \tau_k)$ is ergodic, apply Theorem 2.2 to get $\frac{1}{N_l - M_l} \sum T^n f_1 \otimes T^{2n} f_2 \otimes \cdots \otimes T^{kn} f_k \to \prod \int f_i d\mu$ in $L^2$.

nodes.name: Multiply by f_0 and Integrate
nodes.statement: Multiply by $f_0(x)$, integrate, and rewrite to obtain genericity of $\nu_{k+1}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Roth Theorem (ergodic)
nodes.statement: By Lemma 3.4, the result for arbitrary ergodic systems reduces to Kronecker systems. For Kronecker systems, define $\psi(z') = \int f(z) f(z' z) f(z'^2 z) dm_G$; by unique ergodicity (Lemma 3.6) and continuity (Lemma 3.7) of $\psi$, the Cesaro limit equals $\int \psi dm_G > 0$.

nodes.name: Reduce to Kronecker via Lemma 3.4
nodes.statement: By Lemma 3.4, the limit for arbitrary ergodic system equals limit on the Kronecker factor.

nodes.name: Form Kronecker Average Function
nodes.statement: Set $\psi(z') = \int f(z) f(z z') f(z z'^2) dm_G(z)$ for nonneg $f \in L^\infty(G)$.

nodes.name: Apply Unique Ergodicity
nodes.statement: By Lemma 3.6, the average $\frac{1}{N-M} \sum \psi(g_0^n)$ converges to $\int \psi dm_G$.

nodes.name: Conclude Positivity
nodes.statement: $\psi$ is continuous (Lemma 3.7), nonnegative, and $\psi(e) > 0$, so $\int \psi dm_G > 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Distal Multiple Recurrence
nodes.statement: By induction on the order of the distal system. Base case (order 0) trivial. Inductive step: a system of order $n+1$ is a factor of a strict group extension of a system of order $n$ (Theorems 8.1, 8.3); reduce to Proposition 11.4.

nodes.name: Base Case (Order 0)
nodes.statement: All measures reduce to a single point in the case of order 0 and the theorem is trivial.

nodes.name: Reduce to Group Extension Step
nodes.statement: Use Theorem 8.3: a distal system of order $n+1$ is a factor of an ergodic group extension of a distal system of order $n$. Use Theorem 8.1: ergodic group extension is strict for smaller group.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 11.4
nodes.statement: Apply the group-extension induction step (Proposition 11.4) to complete the inductive step.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 11.4 (Group Extension Step)
nodes.statement: By contradiction: assume $\mu_d^k \not\prec \mu_*^k$. Use $\Phi: Y \to L^1(G)$, find $\phi$ in support of distribution, define set $A$ of $y$ where $\Phi_y$ is close to $\phi$. Use averaging operator $Q$ over diagonal subgroup, apply Lemmas 11.5-11.12 to derive contradiction.

nodes.name: Setup: Function $\Phi$ and its Distribution
nodes.statement: Define $f$ as a product of all $f_i$, then $f: Y \times G \to [0,1]$ defines $\Phi: Y \to L^1(G)$ via $\Phi_y(g) = f(y,g)$, with probability distribution on $L^1(G)$ having non-zero $\phi$ in its support.

nodes.name: Construct Approximate Set A
nodes.statement: Set $a = \int \phi^k dm_G$, $A = \{y : \|\Phi_y - \phi\| < a/4k\}$, and choose nbhd $U$ of identity such that $\int |\phi(g_1 g) - \phi(g)| dm_G < a/4k$ for $g_1 \in U$.

nodes.name: Lower Bound on $Q(f^{\otimes k})$
nodes.statement: On $(A \times U)^k$, $Q(f \otimes \cdots \otimes f) > a/4$, hence $Q(f \otimes \cdots \otimes f) \geq \frac{a}{4} \chi_{(A \times U)^k}$.

nodes.name: Compare Both Sides via Convolution
nodes.statement: Pick $V$ small enough that $V V^{-1} \subset U$, set $f' = \chi_{A \times V}$, derive $\int Q(f^{\otimes k}) d\mu_*^k \geq c \int (f'^{\otimes k}) d\lambda_Q * \mu_*^k$ for some $c > 0$.

nodes.name: Derive Contradiction
nodes.statement: By identity (2) (Lemma 11.12), LHS vanishes; by Lemma 11.11, RHS is positive since $f'$ is not a.e. 0. Contradiction.
